newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita says share spurt normal.
newsitem.headline: Merita says share spurt normal.

text.p: Strong gains in Merita's shares on Wednesday were normal and probably a result of strong foreign demand and a lack of sellers in Finland due to summer holidays, a Merita spokeswoman said.
Asked to comment on sharp gains in the stock, she said demand was sparked by an outperformer stance from U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs and one other house, which she could not name.

"In our view there should be nothing abnormal," Merita spokeswoman Tuulikki Hukari told Reuters. "There is nothing to announce," she said, noting that Merita shares have had similar sudden gains before, last in May.
Merita shares rose over five percent in lively trade soon after the Helsinki bourse opened, but eased by midday to 18.80 markka, still up 0.70 markka or nearly four percent.
Brokers cited strong, possibly speculative, foreign demand.
Merita's session high of 19.30 markka was a 19 percent gain on a recent June 18 trough of 16.20, and just 0.20 markka shy of its intrasession year-high of 19.50 reached on March 12.
